## PM: ACCEPT — the strongest verification work of this session

Both deliverables landed: the gate, and the one measured bump (`@object-ui/plugin-detail` → `^17.1.0`, the only range changed). No range hand-tightened, and no argument that the uniform `^17.0.0` is deliberate appears anywhere — direction taken exactly as triage ruled it.

### You mutated your own new tests, and one survived

This is the part that matters most. After writing the gate's test suite (33 passing), you ran a **5-mutation battery against those tests** — and reported that **one survived**: replacing the "names no lower bound" throw with a permissive `return '0.0.0'`.

That is the single most important safety property in the whole gate. A floor silently read as `0.0.0` is satisfied by **everything**, so the gate would go permanently, confidently green. Your suite could not have caught it, and you found out *why*: every range in your throw-set was rejected earlier, while parsing a comparator, so nothing ever reached that branch. You added upper-bound-only ranges, re-ran the same mutation, and it went red.

New tests are the easiest thing in the world to write vacuously, and almost nobody checks whether their own tests can fail. Reporting a surviving mutant instead of quietly fixing it is what makes the other 32 assertions credible.

### Both resolution hazards handled, and hazard 1 pinned rather than merely avoided

- **Hazard 2 (dual-package).** The gate **fetches the floor version from the registry and walks that tarball's own exports map** under the `import` condition, printing the entry it landed on (`@objectstack/spec@17.0.0 "./ui" [import > types] ./dist/ui/index.d.mts`). It resolves nothing through `node_modules`. `--cross-check` then re-read the `require` half across 45 entry points and confirmed both halves export the same names. And you corroborated the reader independently while designing it: for 17.0.0 `./ui`, the `.d.mts`, the `.d.ts` and the package's own published `api-surface/ui.json` each list **425 names with an empty symmetric difference**.
- **Hazard 1 (root hoisting).** Stated, and cited as evidence **nowhere** — then *pinned*: a test asserts the gate's source (comments stripped) contains no `createRequire`, `require.resolve` or `import.meta.resolve`. Avoiding a trap is good; making it impossible to fall into later is better.

### Control (d) is the one that proves the gate is a gate

(a)–(c) — floor too low goes red naming `ReferenceRailEntry`, green after the bump, red again when lowered back — are the required controls. But you added **(d)** for a reason you stated: *"(a)-(c) alone cannot distinguish a working gate from one hard-wired to one package and one symbol."*

Lowering a **different** package (`@object-ui/core` → `^16.0.0`) produced **five different real symbols across two subpaths**, from both `.d.ts` and `.js` artifacts — `CONTEXT_TOKENS`, `isRuntimeDefaultToken`, `PercentScale`, `SEARCH_VIRTUAL_TYPES`, `DATE_RANGE_PRESETS`. And it printed *"no published 16.x carries every symbol it references; the spec side is what is wrong"* rather than inventing a bump it could not justify. A gate that knows when it cannot answer is worth more than one that always produces a number.

Control (b) also proved the floor is read **per package** (17.1.0 for plugin-detail's `./ui` and `./data`, 17.0.0 for the rest), not globally — which is the property the whole design rests on.

### Two self-corrections, both volunteered

- **The UMD/CJS exclusion guard** first scanned raw file **text** and produced 30 findings across 15 packages — every one a doc comment. Rewritten to scan string **literals** via the parser: all 30 vanish, the real question survives, and a test pins the prose case with those exact strings. Text-scanning a code question is the defect class this lane cleared in #5988; catching it in your own first draft is the lesson landing.
- **A number written from memory** (473 exported names in 17.1.0) into the changeset, re-measured to **442**, corrected before commit. Small, and exactly the kind of thing that becomes a quoted-forward falsehood — this session has now corrected two of those on other cards.

### Judgment calls I'm endorsing

- **Population re-derived**: 19 published packages declare the spec consumer-facing (one smaller than the card's table — `providers` is gone as of PR #6048, as the order warned), plus 8 that declare it only in `devDependencies`, which floors nobody and correctly stays `check-phantom-dependencies.mjs`'s question. Drawing that line explicitly is what keeps the gate from over-reaching.
- **No `pull_request` trigger**, wired to the publish path plus a nightly alarm, because the criterion is artifact-level and needs a full build — the trade the 2026-08-16 ruling on #4846 already settled. And **a test fails if it is ever added to a workflow carrying that trigger**, so the reasoning is enforced rather than remembered.
- **Changeset `patch`**, with #5753's changeset named as the in-repo precedent, and `minor` correctly refused because `pnpm-lock.yaml` still resolves 17.2.0 on that edge — nothing a consumer installs today changes. That is the honest reading of a floor bump.

The `ci-cd-pipeline.md` section was required by `ci-cd-pipeline-doc.test.ts` (which went red until added), and its sibling ratchet then caught a frozen dependency-range literal in your first draft of that prose — removed, and the page points at `packages/plugin-detail/package.json` instead. Two ratchets doing exactly what they were built for.

### Follow-up

**#6078** filed and correctly not folded in: `scripts/invoked-as.mjs`'s header names `scripts/check-entry-guard.mjs` as the gate enforcing its single-spelling rule — **that file does not exist anywhere in the repo**, while 27 hand-typed `process.argv[1]` guards remain in the shape that header documents as going silently inert through a symlink. Several are blocking gates. Nothing fails today; what is broken is the claim, which reads to the next session as "already converted and enforced". Same declared≠actual class this lane has been clearing all day, and it is the third such false-claim-about-tooling finding this round (with #6069 and #6074).

### Landing

⏳ CI converging on `e3f610f9a`. The self check-in verifies every-check-green and lands it.
